title: Payment output preserves selected date and artifact-version context
question: Compare supplied execution dates, grouping dates, wall-clock substitutions and selected schema/namespace.

evidence.title: The execution date in a payment file must follow the selected context
explanation: Creditors are grouped by requested execution date, but Transfer.toXML does not emit that grouping date: the ordinary branch uses 1999-01-01 and the alternate format comparison omits pain. The base schema label also changes according to wall-clock date.

No XML was generated or schema checked. Exact bank/scheme obligations are not inferred from comments. Supplied execution date, format namespace, wall-clock schema selection and message identity need separate deterministic policy.

evidence.title: ex-money: calendar subscription credit uses effective-date denominator and explicit proration policy

functions.name: lib/money/subscription/plan.ex def new(%Money{} = price, interval, interval_count) guarded implementation

explanation: Subscription credit combines interval length measured from the effective date with remaining days measured from the current interval. Price and period proration use distinct carry/rounding policies.
The denominator and numerator reference different dates by construction. Monthly preferred-day adjustment is explicit, while yearly replacement and plan count admission have separate gaps.

Selected proration mode, explicit effective/current start dates and intended valid positive plan interval; source also admits zero/negative integer counts. A calendar-month change can make effective-date denominator differ from the current interval length; a yearly Feb29 replacement is not date-validated. These are not universal subscription rules. explanation: The ordinary business-day list searches one successor after appending its final eligible date; a cached calendar bounds-checks every queried date.
The loop advances even after the last included endpoint. A request whose output is inside the cache can therefore still require calendar data outside it.

evidence.title: DateTime plus a business-day period discards time of day
explanation: DateTime plus/minus BDay explicitly converts the timestamp to Date before applying business-day arithmetic.
The conversion discards clock information as an intentional date-only overload; no clock-preserving or timezone-aware operation follows from it.

DateTime operands and the defined BDay overload, with caller acceptance of a Date result.
